limitations: WER, CER, and boundary measurements are controlled-excerpt observations, not general performance claims.
Line schedules select the evaluation range but do not prompt or otherwise supply reference text to the provider.
Nearest-line-boundary error is not segment assignment accuracy.
Only one provider candidate is available in this slice.
Hidden analytical references were not read.
The initial provider exposes one decoding candidate only.
Exponentiated average log probability is derived and uncalibrated; it is not a correctness probability.
Provider-native timestamps have no independent timing score.
The optional MIT-licensed package and model are installed separately and are not redistributed by this repository.

reference_policy: Public project-authored line text and schedules prepared before provider selection; evaluation excerpt is L001-L005.

results.hypothesis: Good evening. This is the Riverton Evening Access Forum. We are discussing one proposal, a six-month weekday pilot that would keep the community center open until 10 p.m. instead of 8p. M. Mara Chen supports the pilot. Daniel Price opposes authorizing it in its current form. I will ask both participants to use the evidence packet provided before this forum. Mara, please give your opening position. The center should authorize the six-month pilot. During each of the last six months, staff recorded between 36 and 44 arrivals after the last admissible entry time. The pilot survey also found 74 respondents who said they would use the center after eight at least once per week. We have a real access problem, and the grant can pay the projected additional cost during the pilot. Daniel, your opening position. The Board should not authorize the proposal yet. The survey is voluntary. The arrival log may count the same people repeatedly. and Friday security has not been confirmed. The proposal may be worth testing eventually. But the current record does not show that the full five-day pilot is ready.
